text:
Diego: Heads up — a customer hit a weird missing-items bug during onboarding. They were using the JS sample app which launches 8 parallel page fetches and some pages returned 429 intermittently. The Promise.all pattern aborted the whole run and we lost cursor progress.

Maya: thanks Diego. That pattern is unfortunately common in examples. Is this the quickstart repo sample?

Diego: yes, quickstart/examples/paginate. Code looks like:

```
const pages = Array.from({length: 8}, (_, i) => i)
await Promise.all(pages.map(p => client.list({page: p})))
```

When page 2 returns 429 for a couple seconds, the SDK retry middleware just retries independent requests which compounds the burst.

Lin: SDK parity note: Python has a built-in limiter/semaphore + token-bucket in the client by default. JS currently relies on users to add p-limit. We should mirror Python defaults: conservative concurrency (4) and an optional token bucket.

Priya: agree. UX-wise the sample app should show the safe pattern and call out "why". New users copy paste these examples into production.

Maya: also seeing an auth-refresh interaction in our logs: when a token refresh happens while retries are in flight some retries succeed with old token then 401 and we treat it as a fatal error for that page. We should make the paginated helper preserve page state and treat 401/429 as retryable (with limits).

Diego: quick reproducible script I used (mock server that returns 429 on odd pages for first 2 attempts):

```
for i in {1..20}; do \
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "http://localhost:8080/list?page=$((i%6))" &\
done
wait
```

When running against the naive parallel sample we abort ~30% of the time and miss items.

Lin: proposal: SDK changes (small breaking-surface but opt-in flags):
- add client options { defaultConcurrency: 4, tokenBucket: { rate: 20 }, honorRetryAfter: true }
- implement lightweight semaphore + in-memory token bucket
- update paginate helper to keep per-page cursors and retry transient errors before aborting
These should be backwards compatible if defaults are conservative.

Priya: For samples: change quickstart to use streaming pagination or p-queue with concurrency 4 and include a comment linking to docs about backpressure. Also add a short README note in onboarding: "If you see consistent 429s, reduce concurrency and enable honorRetryAfter".

Maya: from infra side we will try to add Retry-After for 429s for short, controlled backoffs. Still want client-side limits though — server headers are not always present (some proxies strip them).

Lin: I'll sketch PRs: 1) sdk/js: add Semaphore and TokenBucket modules + tests; 2) sdk/js: paginate helper update to be "safePaginate" that keeps page state; 3) examples/quickstart: replace Promise.all with p-queue pattern and docs note.

Diego: Can you also add a small e2e that uses the mock server returning intermittent 429s and asserts no items lost? That will catch regressions.

Lin: yes — test plan: mock returns 429 for first N attempts on odd pages; assert final merged list length equals expected. Mark as flaky-test-exempt when stable.

ci-bot: pipeline queued for lin/add-semaphore-tokenbucket (sha: f9b2d1)

Priya: I'll open a doc PR for quickstart and a short onboarding note. tagging docs team for a blurb on "backpressure and pagination".

docs-bot: created docs draft at docs/backpressure-pagination.md (internal)

Maya: one more thing — add telemetry: emit a client-side metric when we do more than X retries for a page, and include concurrency config in telemetry so SRE can distinguish user config vs SDK default.

Lin: good call. We'll emit metrics: sdk.retries.page and sdk.concurrent.requests with labels.

Diego: thanks all. This should reduce PLG friction. I'll update the onboarding issue with links to PRs once ready. :thumbsup:
